items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — jumped straight to 'How can I help you?'
No real agenda statement — 'let me just get some info from you' with no rough timeframe for the call

Probe was thin for a 3,926 sqft home: never asked about additional rooms/garage/storage (the home gym only surfaced because the customer volunteered it at the very end), no box count, no additional stops, no storage stops, no parking/access or walk-distance question, no 'anything you're worried about?' stressor question
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned — and the customer explicitly raised concerns about who handles his wife's belongings and about expensive items
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch — said 'we don't have any additional fees' but never enumerated no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no transportation or assembly fees
Clock: never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and never stated the 2.5-hour minimum (only the 15-minute proration)
No 'does that make sense?' sense-check anywhere in the call
Never gave a time range for the service actually booked — the 6-8 hour and 5.5-6 hour ranges were both for packing scenarios; the customer ended up setting the 8-hour expectation himself
No Save Your Ass prep speech — no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip
Quoted the Saturday rate ($436) first and had to walk it back to the Sunday rate ($404) later, after the customer had already done the math out loud
Booking close: no 'reply with any corrections', no mention of a bolded detail list at the top of the email, no hours or how to reach us
No insurance/valuation explanation at all (No Worries or 60¢/lb) on a call where the customer twice raised handling and damage concerns
top_strength: Outstanding rapport and commercial instinct — he proactively volunteered that Sunday rates are cheaper than Saturday ($404 vs $436) without being asked, and he handled a tricky load-only/out-of-state scenario (waiver, blankets, customer-supplied trucks) cleanly enough that the customer said 'you've been great' and booked on the spot rather than calling other companies.
coaching_note: Landon closes on personality but skips the scorecard. The single biggest fix: run the full differentiator block every time — No Worries $2,000 coverage, On-Time Guarantee, and the 2.5-hour minimum/clock-starts-on-site explanation. This customer directly asked about protecting his belongings and Landon answered with crew vetting instead of the damage coverage that would have sealed it.
phone_presence_notes: Genuine warmth and humor throughout ('you are my kind of guy man'), used Blake's name four times, and the customer reciprocated with 'you've been great' and booked to avoid calling anyone else — held back from a 5 by heavy verbal clutter and repeated filler ('okay, cool, cool, cool').
audio_review_reason: Transcript shows heavily fragmented, overlapping speech on the rep's side — worth confirming on audio whether pace and clarity are genuinely an issue or just transcription artifacts, since that drove the Section 9 clarity deduction.
